Subject: BrightCart — live response slowdowns on streaming/chat (incident & customer actions)

Hi Samira,

Quick note from Redwood on the latency you saw this morning for BrightCart's live-assist flow. We observed an elevated token service latency on a small subset of edge shards that serve streaming/chat responses; that surfaced as delayed first-chunk delivery and sporadic chunk gaps for ~18 minutes between 08:45–09:03 PDT. Impact: 8% of your live sessions saw delayed first-streams; no messages were dropped and fallback responses completed within 6–12s.

What we're doing now:
- Routing affected traffic away from the degraded edge pool; automated fallback to full-response (polling) was enabled immediately.
- Throttled batching for long-conversation sessions to reduce KV-cache pressure.
- Telemetry capture: we've attached per-session traces (brightcart_latency_telemetry.zip) and a short mitigation playbook.

Customer actions you can take right away (low-effort):
1) Enable short-poll fallback in your client for streaming endpoints: set stream_poll_fallback=true and poll_interval=1500ms.
2) Reduce client-side streaming window: set max_open_request_tokens=256 for sessions with lots of tool calls.
3) If you can tolerate slightly lower throughput, pin to the medium model variant (redwood-medium-v1) for a subset of non-critical sessions until we confirm full recovery.

I'll run a brief post-incident review and share the follow-up tomorrow with root cause and permanent mitigations. In the meantime, if you'd like a call right now we can jump into a quick troubleshooting session — available in 20 minutes.

Sorry for the disruption; we'll get this sorted quickly.

Thanks,
Logan Wright

Hi Samira —

Short answers:
- Correctness: we saw delays only. Responses that completed were unchanged in content; there were no truncated outputs or hallucinations noted in the sampled traces.
- SSO sessions: the issue tracked to an edge shard in our us-west region; EU-proxied sessions that traversed us-west were more likely to hit the affected pool. We have already routed EU-proxied traffic to healthy pools while we finish the clean-up.

Runbook (ops-safe, minimal risk) — steps you can perform now:
A) Enable client poll fallback (recommended immediate):
   - Config flag: stream_poll_fallback = true
   - poll_interval_ms = 1500
   - keep_stream_keepalive_ms = 5000
B) Reduce open-token window on long-lived sessions:
   - max_open_request_tokens = 256 (from 1024)
C) Temporary model pin:
   - route 10% of traffic to redwood-medium-v1 until we confirm shard stability
D) If you see persistent gaps after these changes, turn on request-level tracing: request_trace=true and send traces to the Redwood ingestion endpoint included in the playbook.

Attachment attached: brightcart_streaming_mitigation_playbook.pdf (step-by-step toggles, sample curl commands, and npm/JS client snippets).

We'll keep monitoring and I'll post an initial timeline within two hours. Setting up a 30-minute sync for 10:00 PDT (I'll send an invite).

—Marissa

Subject: BrightCart incident 2028-04-21 — post-incident summary & next steps

Hi Samira — thanks again for the quick coordination and for doing the client-side toggles. Summary and follow-ups below.

What happened (short):
- Root cause: a kernel-level memory fragmentation issue in an older GPU driver version on a small set of us-west edge hosts caused token emission jitter. The jitter amplified when many sessions shared large KV caches.
- Impact window: 2028-04-21T08:45–2028-04-21T09:03 PDT.
- Client-visible symptoms: delayed first-chunk delivery and intermittent chunk gaps; no content corruption.

Immediate mitigations completed:
- Traffic re-routed off the affected hosts within 5 minutes.
- Autoscale pre-warm injected to absorb mid-sized bursts.
- Customer recommended steps executed (poll-fallback + pin to redwood-medium-v1 for 10% traffic).

Permanent fixes and timeline:
- Kernel/driver upgrade and a tighter garbage compaction cadence rolled to the affected pool (complete).
- Serving runtime change: improved KV-cache eviction heuristics to avoid high shared-cache pressure (deploying this week).
- New canary: synthetic first-chunk latency monitors per-region (live by 2028-04-28).

Follow-ups we will do for BrightCart:
1) Share a short postmortem doc (attached/redwood_postmortem_2028-04-21.md) with traces and MTTD/MTTR metrics.
2) Schedule a 45-minute technical review with your platform team (we propose 2028-04-25 09:00 PDT).
3) Optionally run a joint load test to validate the KV-cache heuristics (we can run this in our sandbox next week).

If that schedule works I will send calendar invites. Apologies again for the disruption — appreciate the partnership while we fixed it.

Ben Carter
Sr. Incident Manager | Redwood Inference
